An honest grade: a fixed wake anchor, caffeine cutoff, morning light and a bedtime ritual are hard CBT-I evidence, and that is the skeleton of this plan. The \"15 minutes every 3 days\" ladder is clinical jet-lag practice, not a law — its value is that every step is too small to fail. Micro-tasks, check-ins and reviews are behaviour design: they help you execute, they don\'t change your physiology. I\'m not a doctor — for persistent sleep-onset insomnia, heavy snoring or uncontrollable daytime sleepiness, see a sleep clinic.

That is deliberate. What really changes on day 1 is not your sleep time but the wake anchor (immovable) and the wind-down ritual. Your body clock still calls 1:30 \"night\", so going to bed at 23:00 on day one means lying awake for 2.5 hours. The ladder: hold the status quo for 2 days → then 15 minutes earlier every 3 days → target reached on the last day.

Bedtime is a ceiling, not a task — if you\'re sleepy, sleep earlier; if you\'re not, slide 15-30 minutes later. The one thing that never moves is the wake time. Just beware of getting into bed too early: for someone used to 1:30, 21-23:00 is the body clock\'s wakefulness peak, so falling asleep at 9 burns your sleep pressure in the first half of the night → you surface at 3 or 4. Catch the sleepiness instead: do something low-stimulation (warm light, paper book, stretching) until 22:30, then get into bed. If you do wake early, no phone, no lights — lie in the dark until the wake anchor.

Without a wristband, sleep onset is genuinely unmeasurable — that is a physiology problem, not an app bug. The app reads your usage stats for \"last screen-on/screen-off of the night\" as an upper bound (last screen 00:58 → estimate 01:00). Memory after you put the phone down is unreliable; the system log is not. In reviews look at the trend and the bound, not the minutes.

Still awake after 20 minutes in the dark → shift position and keep lying there; during the plan, don\'t get up to work or scroll. Several nights in a row waking at 3-4 with a wrecked day → that is CBT-I stimulus-control territory, see a doctor, and slow the target down (15 minutes a week).

No blame — the plan is a living thing, and when a streak breaks you change the parameters and continue; that isn\'t failure. One bad night: change nothing, today stays as planned (the anchor is waking), and tonight follows the scheduled step. Several nights, or your life rhythm shifted: adjust the plan (loosen for 2-3 days, then pull back). Don\'t \"start over from scratch\" — editing parameters costs far less than restarting.
Keep weekends within ±30 minutes. Social jet lag can wipe out two weeks of progress in one go. If you\'re really exhausted, a nap of ≤20 minutes, not later than 15:00.

The every-7-days checkpoint is the \"Weekly review\" event in your calendar. Last night\'s score and your streak on the Home tab are already the minimal review; for more detail, read me this stretch of check-in trend (or set a key so I can read the data), and we decide the adjustment together.

Too slow: widen the step (e.g. 20 minutes every 3 days) — you\'ll get odd times like 1:10. Too fast (more than 30 minutes lying awake two nights running): drop back one step for 3 days, then continue.
